case_024:
coastal_overlook + elevated_horizon + faint_depth_haze all visible (railing overlook, high horizon line, soft hazy sea); but deep_neutral_accent color_continuity fails — pixel check confirms R=G=B across the whole frame (all three seeds are fully desaturated grayscale, not merely a muted neutral palette), a real rendering defect not seen on any other row of this sheet. -- overturned at full resolution: test_id resolved via manifest: case_024 → style_id "background_coastal_overlook_elevated_horizon_faint_depth_haze_deep_neutral_accent_complete_background" → items P7000070/71/72 (seeds 1001/2002/3003).

Full-resolution inspection of all three image_01.png files (1024x1024) confirms coastal_overlook (railing overlook over the sea), elevated_horizon (high horizon line), and faint_depth_haze (soft hazy sea/sky) are all correctly rendered, matching the thumbnail's positive read.

The color_continuity concern does not hold at full resolution. A pixel-level check (no saturation_screen.json exists for this run, so the raw-pixel test was used instead) shows R, G, B channels are NOT identical: max per-pixel channel difference is 14-20 (of 255) across the three seeds, with 15-29% of pixels showing a channel diff >2, and HSV saturation reaching up to 1.0 in localized regions (mean saturation 0.018-0.024, median 0.008-0.012 per seed). This is a subtle warm-toned muted palette, not literal R=G=B grayscale.

Critically, this saturation profile is not anomalous for this sheet: four other deep_neutral_accent cases from the same manifest (case_001, case_004, case_008, case_012 → P7000001/P7000010/P7000022/P7000034) were sampled and show essentially identical saturation statistics (mean 0.020-0.026, median 0.008-0.012). So case_024 is consistent with — not an outlier from — the rest of the deep_neutral_accent group, contradicting the thumbnail claim that it was "a real rendering defect not seen on any other row of this sheet."

Conclusion: this was a thumbnail-compression artifact (JPEG/downscale compression crushing already-low chroma toward apparent gray), not a genuine desaturation defect. The muted neutral look is the deep_neutral_accent palette rendering as designed. Case_024 should be released from hold.
